catalog_quote: Leslau 1958 p. 4: "Any syllable of the Harari noun or verb can be accented, but the accent has no phonemic value in Harari." ... Sec. 1(a): "The form of type A is säbära. It is characterized by three radicals, the first two radicals having the vowel ä while the vowel of the last radical is a. The accent is on the second syllable (sabara), but for the sake of convenience will not be marked in the verbs listed below." Wagner 1997 p. 488: "Peculiar Phenomena. Neither stress nor tones are phonemic in Harari."

audit.recode_to: Weight-sensitive right-edge tendency (non-phonemic): stress the final syllable if it is closed (CVC#), otherwise the penult — i.e. house 'final-if-heavy(closed)-else-penultimate', two-syllable right window, heavy = closed syllable, stated as a tendency ('tendencija', 'kak pravilo'). Source: Vizirova 2013 p. 419 sec. 2.1.2, reporting Leslau 1963 Etymological Dictionary of Harari, Introduction. Leslau 1958's type-A perfect säbära (penult, open final) and Vizirova's sabára are consistent with it. Grade should be marked second-hand (survey chapter quoting Leslau 1963) until the 1963 Introduction or Beniam 2013 is read; keep the 'not phonemic' notes from Leslau 1958/Wagner 1997.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding sentences are verbatim in the held scanned files at the stated pages (Leslau 1958 p. 4 line 508; Sec. 1(a) line 739 with disclosed diacritic restoration; Wagner 1997 p. 488 lines 31608-9). (2) Deciding source: a 1958 verb-morphology monograph plus a 1997 handbook sketch, neither of which treats stress placement; UNDETERMINED was an honest reading of those two, but they are not the best available. (3) fetched sources now: the open ILING RAN PDF of Jazyki mira: Efiosemitskie jazyki (2013); Vizirova's Harari chapter p. 419 states that stress is weak and non-distinctive but, following the Introduction to Leslau's 1963 Etymological Dictionary, tends to fall on a closed final syllable and otherwise on the penult, with 9 + 13 accent-marked examples. That is a computable positional rule and moves the record out of UNDETERMINED. Beniam Mitiku 2004 MA (AAU, fetched sources) is sile

sources.quote: '2.1.2. Dinamicheskoe udarenie v X.ja., kak i v drugix efiosemitskix jazykax, vyrazheno slabo. Smyslorazlichitel'noj funkcii udarenie ne imeet ... Pravila postanovki udarenija v X.ja. sistematicheski ne izuchalis'. Kak sleduet iz vvedenija k etimologicheskomu slovarju Leslau, imeetsja tendencija k postanovke udarenija na poslednij slog, esli on zakrytyj: adáb, basár, idṓč, dufā́n, birzā́z, buskumā́t, aḥattā́ň, ēlád, dīnát. Esli poslednij slog otkrytyj, udarenie, kak pravilo, padaet na predposlednij slog: báka, sabára, agáda, diladála, adári, ḫā́na, mṓta, ā́ḳa, ā́da, afṓča, gā́yya, dū́da, fuṭū́
